reuse.why: Adds getWorstCaseAmount and uses it at every site, but the existing getScheduledAmount already handles missing, numeric and ranged amounts, and the five sites keep their own null/number/range dispatch instead of calling it.

duplication.why: The range rule now has one definition, but the change leaves the 'missing ? 0 : number ? value : range' dispatch copied at four sites (schedules/app.ts twice, forecast, preview) plus schedule-template, alongside getScheduledAmount, which does the same.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount, where both server and client can import it.

scope.why: Only the rule, its call sites, a test and a release note change; one comment is awkwardly line-wrapped.

maintainability.why: A future change to the range rule is one edit, though a change to how missing or numeric amounts are planned would still have to touch each copied dispatch.

bypasses_abstraction.where: updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule (schedules/app.ts), normalizeSchedule (forecast-schedules.ts), computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and schedule-template keep their own amount dispatch instead of calling getScheduledAmount

disguised_duplication.where: The leftover per-site dispatches are pre-existing near-identical copies, not reshaped by this diff

one_place.where: getWorstCaseAmount in shared/schedules.ts, used by getScheduledAmount and by all five server/shared sites that previously computed the midpoint
